3　The Nature of Drugs

李君儒者也，胡以辑本草？余授李君业儒者也，胡为李君叙本草？
——罗文英《本草原始》序（1612）
Student Li is a Confucian scholar. Why did he write a book on
bencao
? I taught Student Li Confucian learning. Why am I writing a preface for his
bencao

?
—Luo Wenying, preface to
Bencao yuanshi

河南乡试每三年取中举人80至90名。通常至少有一名出自杞县——一座名字见于古代史册的古城。年成好时，一县可出数名举人。明代，许多杞县举人后来又在会试中夺得进士高第。其中，罗文英格外幸运，在万历三十四年（1606）与三十五年（1607）连捷两试。罗在中央衙门任职，正谋求升迁至都察院的理想职位，希望以直言清正立名。当他得知旧日门生李中立撰写了一部以本草为主题的著作，并请他作序时，罗文英决定再给李生上一课，讲讲事物的正当次序。
Every three years, the Henan provincial civil service examination yielded 80–90 successful candidates (
juren

). Usually at least one candidate hailed from Qi County, a historic town whose name had appeared in ancient historical annals. In good years, it might produce several successful candidates. During Ming times, many Qi County juren did go on to win the high degree of jinshi in the metropolitan examination. Among them, Luo Wenying was particularly fortunate to pass the two consecutive examinations in Wanli 34 (1606) and 35 (1607). Serving in a central governmental office, Luo had his eye on a promotion to a desirable position in the censorate, where he would make his name as an outspoken and upright man. When he learned that a former pupil named Li Zhongli wrote a book on the subject matter of bencao—and requested a preface from him—Luo decided to give Li another lecture on the proper order of things.
罗文英以上引那段话开篇，把本草之学与儒家之学的概念对立起来。随后，他又巧妙地转过话头，为双方寻找调和的基础：
Luo Wenying opened his preface with the quote above, pitting the study of bencao against the very concept of Confucian learning. He then deftly came around to find a ground for conciliation:
要以物而物睇之，物何与于我？物而象睇之，即一根一茎，一飞一走一泳，以及块然凝黯然呈者，曷非吾性之森罗而法象乎？

If one sees Things as Things, how can they have anything to do with myself? If one sees Things as Images, then a wooden root, a grassy root, a gesture of flying, wandering, and swimming, the silent coagulations and dim appearances . . . all these are nothing but the awesome manifestations of my own Nature.
罗文英对门生这番不寻常努力的认可带着几分调侃，可以从两方面来读。它既反映了区分儒家之学与医学、药学等单纯技术追求的持久污名，也反映了一种日益强劲的、试图跨越此类藩篱的动向。罗文英能够借助“性”的概念，使对本草的儒学研究成为可能，这也正是明代理学思想的特征。本章以这种对物性的矛盾态度为起点，主张本草与理学自然哲学的交汇，只有在17世纪最初几十年特定的政治与文化条件下才得以发生。

Luo Wenying’s tongue-in-cheek approval of his pupil’s unusual endeavor can be read in two ways. It reflected the persistent stigma that distinguished Confucian learning from mere technical pursuits, such as medicine and pharmacy, but also an increasingly strong movement toward overcoming such barriers. It was also characteristic of Ming neo-Confucian thought that Luo was able to make a Confucian study of bencao possible through the concept of nature (
xing

). This chapter takes this ambivalence toward the nature of things as its starting point, and argues that the confluence of bencao and neo-Confucian natural philosophy only took place under specific political and cultural conditions in the first decades of the seventeenth century.
李中立也在万历四十年（1612）赢得了令人艳羡的乡试功名。此后，他的公共生活再无记载，但其书法与绘画保存在他所著的《本草原始》中。尽管李中立独自“纂辑并书画”全书，他却没有自撰序言来说明方法或志向。
现代学者断定，李中立的本草大量依据《本草纲目》，很可能是受这部极新的药典成功的启发。然而，李书最突出的仍是其图像的原创性与品质：数百幅药材插图呈现出前人所未见的细节。图文交织的方式，后来的版本已未能保存（图3.1）。
《本草原始》初刻本是杞县紧密的精英网络中地方声望的产物；其新鲜与原创性在后来的版本中消失了。
Student Li Zhongli also won the coveted provincial degree in Wanli 40 (1612). No further records existed of him in public life, yet his calligraphy and drawings are preserved in his
Bencao yuanshi (Original Inquiries of Materia Medica
). Although Li “compiled, wrote, and illustrated” (
zuanji bing shuhua
) the text all by himself, he did not write his own preface to explain his method or aspirations.
Modern scholars have concluded that Li’s bencao relied heavily on
Bencao gangmu

and was likely inspired by the success of this very new pharmacopeia. The pictorial features of Li’s text, however, stood out in their originality and quality: the several hundred illustrations of materia medica showed details unseen in previous works. Pictures and texts were interwoven with each other in a way that later editions failed to preserve (figure 3.1).
The first edition of
Bencao yuanshi
was a product of local prestige in the tightly knit elite network of Qi County; the freshness and originality were lost in subsequent editions.

因此，本章不仅讨论理学内部关于药性的微妙争论，也讨论晚明中国为实践这些理想而作出的众多而多样的尝试。与李中立一样，许多对本草主题发生兴趣的儒家士人，属于在万历朝（1572—1620）后期或其后成长起来的年轻一代。毫不奇怪，他们大多生活并主要活动于江南——明代中国最繁荣、人口最稠密的地区（见地图0.1插图）；但对本草的热情确实也传到了江南之外，李中立的例子便是明证。李中立同样典型的是，他研习医学却不以行医为生。如果这一描述颇合列文森（Joseph Levenson）等人所说的中国文化史上的“业余主义”，那么正如我在导论中所论，我们就需要具体说明，究竟是怎样的地方与个人境遇，使这类智识冒险对他们具有吸引力。

This chapter is thus not only about subtle debates within the neo-Confucian doctrine about the nature of drugs, but also the numerous and diverse attempts to live up to those ideals in late Ming China. Like Li Zhongli, many Confucian literati who took an interest in the subject of bencao belonged to the younger generations who came of age during or after the late decades of the Wanli reign (1572–1620). Not surprisingly, most of them lived and were primarily active in Jiangnan, the most prosperous and populous region of Ming China (see map 0.1 inset); but the enthusiasm for bencao did travel outside Jiangnan, as Li Zhongli’s case exemplifies. Li was also typical in that he pursued medical learning without practicing medicine for a living. If this description fits quite well what Joseph Levenson and others called “amateurism” in Chinese cultural history then, as I discussed in the introduction, we need to specify the local and personal circumstances that made such intellectual adventures appealing to them.

让我在开头也说明一点：本章所讨论的行动者与文本，显然可以、也应当通过宗教的框架来分析。“三教”（儒、释、道）合流是晚明中国的主导文化潮流，本草的吸引力不仅源于理学中特定的性论，也源于17世纪禅宗的复兴。
我在第一章已经提出，雷公炮制文本的再造可以视为道教思想推动的精英养生文化的一部分。缪希雍是一个关键人物，他的作为提升了本草之学在士人中的吸引力；他师从禅宗大师，除医学外还从事堪舆。这里的叙述聚焦于本草知识与明代文化精英之间的互动；这些人共享相同的教育背景，并渴望在公共生活中扮演角色。

Let me also say at the outset: it will become apparent that the actors and texts I discuss in this chapter can, and should, also be analyzed through the framework of religion. Syncretism of the “three teachings” (Confucianism, Buddhism, and Daoism) was a dominant cultural trend in late Ming China, and the appeal of bencao was motivated not only by particular doctrines of nature in neo-Confucianism, but also the revival of Chan Buddhism in seventeenth century.
I have already suggested in chapter 1 that the reinvention of
Master Thunder
texts on the processing of pharmaceuticals can be seen as part and parcel of the elite nurturing life (
yangsheng

) culture fueled by Daoist ideas. Miao Xiyong, a pivotal figure whose exploits boosted the appeal of bencao learning among literati, followed Chan Buddhist masters and practiced geomancy alongside medicine. The narrative here focuses on the interaction between bencao knowledge and the cultural elite of Ming China, who shared a common educational background and aspired to play a role in public life.
物与我
Things and Us

第一章我们看到，12世纪时，药性已成为医者与朱熹一类理学家共同关注的问题。朱熹用大黄之性来说明理在自然中无形而真实的存在，同时也热衷于建构一个性的等级秩序。如果万物都同样禀有性，而世界之理（li）可通过性显现，为何草木禽兽不能也成为觉悟的圣人？人究竟特殊在何处？朱熹的回答是：性并不尽同，每一物都依其特有的禀赋而存在。用他自己的比喻，理如水与日光，处处相同，而分量有别。然而，水或日光的分量不同，会因身体或容器的种类及其摆放位置而显现差异；站在投下阴影的屋檐下，所能接受的光照强度便会减弱。

In chapter 1, we saw that the nature of drugs became an issue of common interest for both physicians and neo-Confucian philosophers like Zhu Xi in the twelfth century. While Zhu Xi used the qualities of rhubarb to illustrate the invisible presence of coherence in nature, he was also keen to construct a hierarchy of natures. If all were similarly endowed with a nature (
xing
) through which the coherence of the world (
li

) could manifest itself, why couldn’t plants and beasts also become enlightened sages? What made human beings special? Zhu Xi’s answer was that not all natures were alike, but each existed with its own particular endowments. In his own metaphor, li, like water and sunlight, was the same everywhere but different in quantity. Different amounts of water or sun, however, would be apparent depending both on the kind of body or vessel and where it was placed; standing underneath a roof that cast a shadow would diminish the intensity of sunlight that could be received.
在朱熹形而上世界存在的巨大等级中，人生来便禀有完整（quan）而无蔽的理，适于道德的完美显现；非人之物则“偏塞”（pianse）。
圣人是最觉悟的人，其性至纯至备；其次是各种不完美的人，但他们仍可向往成圣。最聪慧的动物有时也表现出类人的道德行为：蜂蚁似乎懂得君臣上下之分，猫则像人类父母一样照料幼崽。在道德禀赋的等级上更下一层的是其他动物、植物、岩石与金属——它们的身体又反过来被制成药物。
In the great hierarchy of being in Zhu Xi’s metaphysical world, human beings were born with a complete (
quan
) and unobstructed endowment of li that was conducive to the perfect manifestation of morality, whereas nonhuman things were “partial and obstructed” (
pianse

Sages, the most enlightened people, possessed a nature that was the purest and most perfect of all; then came humans with all sorts of imperfections, who could, nonetheless, aspire to sagehood. The brightest animals sometimes showed humanlike moral behavior: bees and ants behaved as if they knew the hierarchy between lords and serfs, while cats took care of their young like human parents. Further down the hierarchy of moral endowment were other animals, plants, rocks, and metals—whose bodies, in turn, were made into medicine.

因此，朱熹对人性和物性的表述引出了一种自然伦理：人应当顺应自然所赋，尽其所能——“率性”或“尽性”，使为善的潜能尽可能充分地实现。个人被劝勉走上自我发现与自我成全之路。然而，其中的负面含义也十分清楚：通往成圣之路障碍重重，皆源于人不得不与之共存的物质存在中的固有倾向。朱熹规定了男女之间固定的差异，称“妇人之仁，只流从爱上去”，因而软弱。夷狄也好不到哪里去：在朱熹看来，他们是抗拒文明教化的半兽之民。非人之物同样困守于其偏狭独特的本性，其身体如同昏暗的镜子，“中间只有一两点子光”。
这些论说反映了一种冲动：要让共同修习理学的同道确信，他们毕竟生来便禀有优于他者的性。

Zhu Xi’s formulation of human nature and the nature of things therefore invited an ethics of nature: that is, one ought to work with what nature had given, making the most of it—to “let the nature be” (
shuaixing
), or “exhaustively explore one’s nature” (
jinxing

), so that the potential to be moral and good could be realized as fully as possible. An individual was exhorted to follow a path of self-discovery and a life of fulfillment. The negative connotations, however, were also very clear: there were many perils obstructing the path to sagehood, all caused by tendencies inherent within one’s material existence that one could not help but live with. Zhu Xi dictated a fixed difference between men and women, whose nature, in his words, was given to “excessive affection,” and hence weakness. Barbarian peoples (
yidi

) fared no better: for Zhu Xi, they were half-beast beings that resisted the forces of civilization. Nonhuman beings, too, were stuck in their partial, idiosyncratic natures, their bodies resembling a darkened mirror, with “only a few dots of light in the middle.”
These arguments reflected the urge to reassure fellow practitioners of neo-Confucian self-cultivation that they were, after all, already endowed with a superior nature than that of others.
在涵盖宋元明（12至17世纪）的漫长时期里，理学领袖们反复争论性的问题。朱熹及宋代其他思想家的教说，在许多方面提供了多种可能的立场。一条显著的论辩路线围绕何者优先展开：气（qi）还是理（li）。主张“物质的创造性”——用达格玛·舍费尔（Dagmar Schäfer）的话说——优先的观点，使许多人转而关注技术的重要性。
另一些人则试图依据自己的时代调整、复兴道德修习的实践：王阳明（1472—1529）的学说在明中叶的显赫，正说明了这一路径的活力。1506年，王阳明因声援戴铣而被贬（见第二章），他通过对自身道德良知（liangzhi）的内省探究，重新找到了确定性的源泉。王阳明名言“知行合一”，劝勉弟子专注于从“胸中”涌现的直觉之念。
王阳明学说对内省的强调，不应被解释为反对物质性；相反，正如我们将看到的，它鼓励一种更开放的态度，去重新配置朱熹僵硬的性之等级。多数明代儒者都同意，非人之物（wu）与人性探究具有普遍关联。甚至王阳明——那位以“格竹”闻名、宣称通过“格”竹子无法通向道德觉悟的人——也承认，人的存在不能与物之知相割裂。

During the long period encompassing the Song-Yuan-Ming era (the twelfth through seventeenth centuries), leading scholars of neo-Confucian thought repeatedly debated the question of nature. The teachings of Zhu Xi, along with other Song thinkers, offered a range of possible positions on many fronts. One prominent line of argumentation turned on the question of which was primary: matter (
qi
) or coherence (
li
). The view that held the primacy of “material inventiveness,” in Dagmar Schäfer’s words, led many to turn their attention to the importance of technology.

Others sought to adjust and rejuvenate the practice of moral cultivation according to their own times: the prominence of Wang Yangming’s (1472–1529) teaching in mid-Ming times illus- trated the vitality of this approach. Exiled because of his support of Dai Xian in 1506 (see chapter 2), Wang found a renewed source of certainty by devoting attention to introspective investigation of one’s own moral conscience (
liangzhi
). Wang’s famous dictum, “knowledge and action are one” (
zhi xing he yi
), exhorted his disciples to focus on the intuitive thoughts that sprang forth from “within one’s chest.”

The emphasis placed on introspection by Wang Yangming’s teaching should not be interpreted as an argument against materiality: rather, as we will see, it encouraged a more open attitude to reconfiguring Zhu Xi’s rigid hierarchy of natures. Most Ming Confucians agreed on the general relevance of nonhuman things (
wu

) to the exploration of human nature. Even Wang Yangming, who famously announced that there was no path toward moral enlightenment through “investigating” a bamboo plant, acknowledged that human existence could not be severed from the knowledge of things.
16世纪，重要的儒家教师对人性与物性的共通与差异提出了一系列立场。
湛若水关于格物的宏富著述广受欢迎（见第二章），但他没有接受物质居于首位、超出心灵所能把握的观点。然而，湛若水不同意王阳明把心与内省置于对物质世界之知之上，他劝勉弟子通过生活中的各种遭遇去“体认”事物中内在的道德原则。
湛若水有自己的优先次序：作为一位显要的政治家，他沿着政务的轴线构拟格物概念。第二章我们看到，他与其他敢于议政的官员一样，对各种政策立场的道德性持有僵硬意见。因此，我们可以把他的立场视为一种通过执着的制度现实主义来强调道德知识与行动相联系的立场。
A range of positions on the commonality and distinction between human nature and the nature of things thus came to be articulated in the sixteenth century by leading Confucian teachers.
Zhan Ruoshui, whose comprehensive writings on the investigation of things (
gewu

) enjoyed great popularity (see chapter 2), refrained from embracing a primacy of matter as beyond the mind’s grasp. Disagreeing with Wang Yangming’s prioritizing of the mind and introspection over knowledge of the material world, however, Zhan exhorted his disciples to “embody and recognize” (
tiren
) the moral principles immanent in things through various encounters in life.
Zhan had his own hierarchy of priorities: writing as a prominent statesman, Zhan formulated his concept of
gewu

along the axis of governmental affairs. In chapter 2, we saw that he, like other politically outspoken officials, held rigid opinions on the morality of various policy positions. We could therefore consider his position to be one that emphasized the connection of moral knowledge and action through an insistent institutional realism.
16世纪初其他著名教师，如罗钦顺（1465—1547），则更明确地强调物质与物性的重要。用罗钦顺自己的话说，“理一分殊”。
罗钦顺似乎只是改述了朱熹的教说，但栖身于朱熹巨大等级不同阶位上的生物，却被重新表述为共居于世界大图景中的不同（shu）成员。每一物都有其长处与缺陷，这本来就自然且恰当。一些思想家，如王廷相（1474—1544），甚至设想物质存在的多样性可能依据不止一个、且不完全连贯的理而运作。

Other prominent teachers of the early sixteenth century, such as Luo Qinshun (1465–1547), emphasized the importance of matter and the nature of things more explicitly. In Luo’s own words, “Principle is one; its particularizations are diverse” (
li yi fen shu
Though Luo seemed to have merely rephrased Zhu Xi’s teachings, creatures that inhabited different rungs of Zhu’s great hierarchy came to be recast as but different (
shu

) members residing in the great panorama of the world. Each had its virtues and imperfections, which was only natural and appropriate. Some thinkers, such as Wang Tingxiang (1474–1544), even toyed with the idea that the diversity of material existence could function based upon more than one less than completely coherent principle.

在王阳明的晚期弟子邓元锡（1529—1593）身上，我们可以找到一种折衷立场：既承认物质世界的多样性，又不损害人心的优先地位。在一部题为《函史》的类书式文本中，邓元锡通过采择古今作者的广泛著作，力图说明无所不在的道德之理。他从儒家经典开始，继而考察历代正史中的政府制度与卓异人物。这部八十一卷的类书对宇宙论极为敏感（九为阳数之极，九乘九为八十一，象征丰盈与繁盛之极），末卷论“物性”（wuxing）。
非人之物被置于最后，这使该书与朱熹的性之等级相一致；然而邓元锡的叙述却表现出早期文献中罕见的热烈兴趣。邓元锡的主要资料——或许并不意外——是宋代本草药典；如第一章所见，这部药典在16世纪通过印刷广泛流传，对邓元锡而言，它是对外部世界描述的标准参考。

In Deng Yuanxi (1529–93), a late disciple of Wang Yangming, we can find an eclectic position that acknowledged the diversity of the material world without compromising the primacy of the human mind. In an encyclopedic text titled
Han shi (History in a Casket

), Deng sought to illustrate the omnipresent moral coherence through sampling a wide range of works by both ancient and recent authors. Beginning with Confucian classics, Deng went on to survey governmental institutions and remarkable individuals from dynastic Histories. The eighty-one-volume encyclopedia, constructed with a great sensitivity to cosmology (nine being the greatest yang number, multiplied by nine becoming eighty-one, which represents utmost abundance and efflorescence), ends with a chapter on the “nature of things” (
wuxing

The fact that nonhuman things came last brought this work in line with Zhu Xi’s hierarchy of natures, and yet Deng’s account displayed a passionate enthusiasm rarely seen in earlier sources. The main source for Deng was—perhaps unsurprisingly—the Song bencao pharmacopeia, which, as we saw in chapter 1, became widely available through print in the sixteenth century and served for Deng as the standard reference for descriptions of the external world.

邓元锡接受并赞美宋代本草关于普遍药物物性的构想。他把人与本草所载生物的关系视为“相养相生”。关于“生”的主张显然指药学的有益作用；人之生命之所以可能，正因有物滋养、疗愈我们。对邓元锡而言，能够疗病的药物之存在，提供了宇宙以人为中心的最有力证据；理解这一点，便能发现万物尽性（jin xing）的最大潜能。此外，这种探究是儒者的正当任务，不仅在于遵行天道以成就自身的道德完善，也在于把这种理解应用于君道。据英文底本，他称药物在万物中最精妙、多样而神奇。
其中的迷醉语调并不难察觉。
编者说明：本段末尾对药物的评价根据英文底本转述，邓元锡《函史》所引原句及具体卷叶尚待核对。

Deng accepted the Song bencao’s vision for a universal pharmaceutical objecthood and celebrated it. He saw the relationship between human beings and the creatures documented in bencao as one of “mutual nourishment and regeneration” (
xiang yang xiang sheng
). The claim about regeneration (
sheng

) clearly refers to the beneficial action of pharmacy; human life was possible because of the things that nourished and healed us. For Deng, the existence of drugs that could heal offered the most salient proof that the universe revolved around human beings, and understanding that led to discovery of the maximum potential of nature (
jin xing

) for all creatures. Furthermore, this exploration was the proper task for Confucians not only to achieve their own moral perfection through adherence to the heavenly way, but also to apply this understanding to the lordly art of governance (
jundao
). “Behold medicines,” he wrote, “are they not the most refined, the most varied, and the most divine of beings?”
The overtone of ecstasy is not difficult to detect.

然而，承认物质是知识的潜在来源，并未完全解决认识论问题；因为正如邓元锡所指出的，人与物相互关联的本性并不那么容易显露其真。邓元锡便认为，物的外形（xing）如同加于人心的桎梏，真正的知识必须来自从其深处涌出的直觉。

在此，我们发现了本章开头所引罗文英对本草评论的根源：对罗而言，物质“块然凝黯然呈者”只是无关的噪音，除非人把它们视为自身（人）之性的“法象”（fa xiang）。因此，观看事物的正确方式，是透过它们去看，而不执著于任何感官的干扰。从这一超然立场出发，儒家学者以一种疏离的姿态接触本草中的药学教说。当董其昌（1555—1636）——一位显要人物、业余士人绘画的倡导者——应邀为17世纪初某一版李时珍《本草纲目》作序时，他断言关于药物的真知不可能仅凭感官获得；因此，神农必定是通过宇宙的八象（ba xiang）直觉到他的知识，而非实际品尝各种物质。
我们将会发现，这一主流观点在17世纪之交开始动摇。

Yet the acknowledgement of matter as a potential source of knowledge did not completely solve the question of epistemology, for, as Deng noted, the interconnected natures of people and things did not reveal its truth so easily. Deng Yuanxi, for one, held that the appearances (
xing
) of things were like handcuffs on the mind, and that true knowledge must be derived from intu- ition springing forth from its depths.

Here, we detect the source of Luo Wenying’s comment on bencao that I quoted at the beginning of this chapter: the “silent coagulations and dim appearances” of matter were, for Luo, irrelevant noise unless one contemplated them as the “regular images” (
fa xiang
) of one’s own (human) nature. The proper way of looking at things was thus to look
through

them without holding on to any sensual distractions. From this detached position, Confucian scholars engaged with the teaching of pharmacy in bencao in an aloof manner. When Dong Qichang (1555–1636), a prominent figure and champion of amateur literati paintings, was invited to write a preface for an early seventeenth-century edition of Li Shizhen’s
Bencao gangmu
, he concluded that true knowledge about drugs could not have been obtained through mere senses; the Divine Farmer (
Shennong
) must therefore have
intuited
his knowledge through the eight images (
ba xiang
) of the cosmos, not actual tasting of various substances.
We will discover that this mainstream view started to shift at the turn of the seventeenth century.
东林党人与本草的业余化
Donglin Partisans and the Amateurization of Bencao
撇开学说分歧不谈，晚明精英士人发现自己因在家制作、施送成方成药，而日渐被药物知识的感官面向所吸引。精英当然一向重视家人的切身康健，会设法获取最好的药材与炮制手段。然而，在自己的庄园中设立私人“药室”（yaoshi，一个带有炼丹意味的雅称）的风气，在明中叶至晚期的江南尤为显著。
据英文底本，名画家仇英（1494—1552）患慢性关节痛，曾在信中向一位赞助人索取其家中新制的贵重丸药。
高濂（约活动于16世纪后期）是畅销书《遵生八笺》的作者，他对如何布置、维护这样一处空间给出了详细指示：

Doctrinal differences aside, the elite literati of the late Ming found themselves gravitating toward the sensual aspects of pharmaceutical knowledge through making and dispensing compound medicines at home. The elite had, to be sure, always invested in the personal wellbeing of their family members by securing the best ingredients and the means to prepare them. Yet the trend toward setting up private “pharmaceutical chambers” (
yaoshi
, a fancy term with alchemical overtones) at one’s own estate became especially pronounced in mid- and late-Ming Jiangnan.
The famous painter Qiu Ying (1494–1552), suffering from chronic joint pain, once asked one of his patrons in a letter for an expensive pill “newly-prepared at your household.”
Gao Lian (fl. late sixteenth century), bestselling author of the celebrated
Eight Discourses on the Art of Living
, gave detailed instructions on how to equip and maintain such a space:

只需说，精英士人通过自己制作、服用药物，有充分理由格外关注物的物质性。与必须维持盈利性诊务的医者不同，精英家庭在奢侈稀奇的药物上不惜重金。除了如何在家设置药室的说明，高濂这部过好生活的指南还提供大量方剂，供读者自行尝试。正是这同一批受众——士大夫家庭以及效仿他们的暴发户——其需求不久将推动制药技术的规范化，并激发对药物物性进行新探究的胃口。

Suffice it to say that the elite literati, through their own experience of making and consuming medicine, had every reason to pay heightened attention to the materiality of things. Unlike physicians who had to sustain profitable practices, elite families spared no expense on extravagant and obscure substances. In addition to instructions on how to set up a pharmaceutical chamber at home, Gao Lian’s guide to living a good life also offered a large number of recipes that his readers could experiment with. It was this same audience—families of scholar-officials, and the nouveau riche who aspired to imitate them—whose demand would soon motivate the codification of pharmaceutical techniques and an appetite for new inquiries into pharmaceutical objecthood.
晚明文化中对自我的讲究呵护，集中体现为对“养生”的关注，与王阳明学派对自我修习的强调有密切关联。
悖论的是，一种本为鼓励士人参与公共生活而发明的学说，竟被翻转过来，为一种近乎自恋的、向内关注自我的执迷提供正当性。这种对公共参与与私人关切之间矛盾的接纳，在本草的业余化中得到表达。
The lavish care of the self in late-Ming culture, as summed up by the concern over the “nurturing of life” (
yangsheng
), bears close connections to the Wang Yangming school’s emphasis on self-cultivation.

Paradoxically, a doctrine invented to encourage the literati’s participation in public life was inverted to justify an inward-looking obsession with the self that came close to narcissism. This embrace of ambivalence between public and private engagements found expressions in the amateurization of bencao.
1638年，居于昆山（见地图0.1插图）的藏书家兼私家出版者葛鼐（1630年举人）得到李中立的本草，将其作为双璧之一刊行新版，另一部是讲军事训练的论著。
葛鼐在序中解释说，战争与医学有许多共通之处：两者都能“驱患苦而活人”。然而从根本上说，一切善都出自个人的道德行动：自私与利他之间本无区别。据英文底本，葛鼐认为，要善用自身，首先必须给予自身应有的尊重。
或许正是受这一学说驱动，葛鼐改动了李中立的版面设计，突出治疗指示，而压低名称与形态部分（图3.1下）。他丝毫不觉得同时以医学与军事之艺的业余爱好者自居有何不妥，并以此向读者宣传这部双璧之作。

In 1638, Ge Nai (juren 1630), a bibliophile and private publisher who resided in Kunshan (map 0.1 inset), obtained Li Zhongli’s bencao and issued a new edition as one of twin volumes, the other being a treatise on military training.

In his preface, Ge explained that war and medicine had much in common: they both could “get rid of suffering and save people’s lives.” Yet fundamentally all goodness emerged from individual moral actions: at root, there was no distinction between selfishness and altruism. In Ge’s own words, “to make good use of oneself, one must first pay due respect to the self.”

Perhaps motivated by this doctrine, Ge Nai altered Li Zhongli’s page design to highlight therapeutic instructions, while downplaying the sections on names and morphology (figure 3.1b). He saw no trouble at all in posing himself as an amateur of both medical and military arts, and advertised this twin-volume to his readers as such.

后来许多人把1630、1640年代以自我为中心的文化视为颓废与败亡的征兆，预示了1644年明朝的覆灭。然而，把葛鼐对自私的辩护视为道德追求轨迹的偏离，却是错误的；它不过是《大学》及其他理学文本所教义理的一种逻辑延伸。这里的要点在于，对自我照护的浓厚兴趣得到财富与身份的支撑，并被时人视为与追求公共善相一致。事实上，个人福祉与公共行动之间的同样等式，在几十年前一场最壮观的政治人格展示——所谓东林党人的兴起与被迫害——中也十分醒目。

Many would later come to see the self-centered culture of the 1630s and 1640s as a sign of decadence and doom, foreshadowing the dynasty’s fall in 1644. Yet it would be wrong to see Ge Nai’s defense of selfishness as an aber- ration from the trajectory of moral pursuits; it was but a logical extension of doctrines taught in
Great Learning

and other neo-Confucian texts. The important point here is that the heightened interest in the care of the self was buttressed by the possession of wealth and status, and was perceived as consistent with the pursuit of the public good. In fact, the same equation between personal wellbeing and public action also figured prominently a few decades earlier in one of the most spectacular displays of personhood in politics—the rise and persecution of the so-called Donglin partisans.
16世纪明廷旷日持久的派系冲突，导致史家达德斯（John Dardess）所称的“道德复兴运动”在17世纪初凝聚成形。
一个特定的重心围绕无锡县（见地图0.1）新修葺的东林书院形成。一批志同道合的儒家学者——或遭罢官，或退居乡里——松散地聚合在书院定期集会，讨论学说问题，同时谋求把同道安插到关键官职，并排挤敌人。据我所知，关于这个群体的卷帙浩繁的研究尚未考察他们对医学、特别是药学的兴趣。书院创始领袖之一高攀龙（1562—1626）常在家配制成药，施予贫民。
另一位资深成员赵南星（1550—1627）从《本草纲目》中抄录笔记，编成一部本草，侧重常用作食物与饮品的药材。
丁元荐（1560—1625）是东林的常客，家居长兴县（见地图0.1插图），对医学尤为关注，喜欢从交游圈中收集效方。1613年，丁元荐刊行了一部这类方剂的汇集，附以每则医案的简短叙述，采用笔记的形式。他特别表彰缪希雍（1546—1627）的卓越医术；这位名医曾为他以及高攀龙等许多东林友人及其家人治病，并慷慨分享方剂。
Protracted factional clashes at the Ming court during the sixteenth century led to the consolidation of what historian John Dardess called an “ethical revitalization movement” in the early 1600s.

A particular center of gravity formed around the newly renovated Donglin Academy located in Wuxi County (map 0.1). A loosely defined group of like-minded Confucian scholars, banished from office or retired at home, held regular meetings at the academy to discuss doctrinal issues, with an eye toward installing like-minded allies into key official positions and eliminating their enemies. The voluminous literature on this group has, to my knowledge, not yet examined their interest in medicine, in particular the matter of pharmacy. Gao Panlong (1562–1626), one of the founding leaders of the Academy, frequently prepared compound medicines at home and donated them to the poor.
Zhao Nanxing (1550–1627), another senior member of the faction, wrote a bencao by taking notes from
Bencao gangmu
, focusing on ingredients commonly used as food and drinks.

Ding Yuanjian (1560–1625), a Donglin regular who lived in his hometown in Changxing County (see map 0.1 inset), was particularly interested in medicine and liked to collect efficacious prescriptions from his social circles. In 1613, Ding published a collection of such prescriptions accompanied by short narratives of each case, in the form of a literary miscellany (
biji

). He credited in particular the brilliance of Miao Xiyong (1546–1627), a master physician who treated him and many other Donglin friends, including Gao Panlong and his family members, and generously shared his prescriptions with them.
缪希雍是何许人？关于他的轶事在下江地区一直流传到18世纪。缪希雍虽是无科举功名的“布衣”平民，却出身常熟县（见地图0.1插图）的“望族”。他早年失去双亲，放弃科举仕进，涉猎堪舆、方术等各种秘术，并一度师从著名的禅宗大师。缪希雍以一副奇士般的醒目相貌（“电目戟髯”）著称，常骑马往来于江南各大市镇，非正式地向官员提供政务建议。正是通过医学，缪希雍得以与东林名士结下友谊，他们“以兄事之”。
他与丁元荐广泛合作编纂医案方集，其中许多故事展示了他的医术。医案集的成功进一步提升了他在江南精英士大夫中的声望；他所到之处，求方者络绎不绝。
Who was Miao Xiyong? Anecdotes about him lingered in the Lower Yangzi region well into the eighteenth century. As a “cloth-clad” (
buyi
) commoner without an examination degree, Miao was nonetheless born into of one of the “finest families” (
jiazu

) of Changshu county (map 0.1 inset). Having lost his parents early on, Miao abandoned the pursuit of an official career and dabbled in all sorts of esoteric arts including geomancy and magic, studying for a while under renowned Chan Buddhist masters. Known for his striking appearance (“electrifying eyes and protruding whiskers”) befitting an “eccentric gentleman” (
qishi

), Miao traveled constantly through the major towns of Jiangnan on horseback, advising officials informally on governmental affairs. It was through medicine that Miao was able to cement his friendship with prominent Donglin scholars, who “treated him as an elder brother.”

He collaborated extensively with Ding Yuanjian on the case-prescription collection in which many tales showcased his skills. The success of the case collection further boosted his reputation among elite scholar-officials of Jiangnan; wherever he traveled, he was ceaselessly sought out for prescriptions.
缪希雍行医的方式令同时代观察者觉得奇特。据底本引述的地方志传记，缪希雍行医不带药囊，只为病人开方，疗效十分显著。
书方这一行为本身，成了缪希雍用来折服观众的炫技表演。常熟文坛领袖钱谦益（1582—1664）在许多年后仍记得这样一幕：

He thinks deeply and observes attentively, as if deep in Chan meditation; now he closes his eyes and falls into hypnosis, and in the next moment he rises with full force, lifting his beard and rolling up sleeves, and proceeds to write a prescription and put together some medicines. He takes command and oversees things, and ideas just spring out from his fingers.
缪希雍还以不顾组方的既定规则著称，他的方剂常令不能理解其配伍的“俗医”惊愕。
这些印象与缪希雍的坚持相合：他要建立一种脱离药铺经营中的私利考量的医疗实践，同时宣称自己对药性有超群的把握，因而临床屡效。
Miao was also known for disregarding the set rules of formula building, and his prescriptions often startled “vulgar physicians” (
suyi
) who could not understand his combination of drugs.

These impressions matched Miao’s insistence on building a medical practice that was detached from the proprietary concerns of shopkeeping, while claiming superior understanding of the nature of drugs that led to clinical success.
1620年代初，年迈的缪希雍迁居金坛县（见地图0.1插图），继续诊病，并与地方士绅交游。在一位年轻弟子（此人还负担他的居所开销）的坚持下，缪希雍同意修订先前刊行的医案集，增加一篇远为详细的药材“炮制”方法。修订本医案集于1622年以缪希雍之名刊行，其中论制药方法的一章很快被单独翻刻为《炮制大法》。
此书所载制药指示的对象并非普通医者，而是精英病人本身；他们更愿意在家中指挥自己的仆人制备药物。史家文树德（Paul Unschuld）观察到，炮制文献在17世纪之交达到“兴趣的顶峰”，这并非巧合。
对手工技术的文本化，源于精英病人实用与哲学兴趣的结合，而非职业标准化。

In the early 1620s, an aging Miao Xiyong moved to Jintan County (map 0.1 inset), where he continued to see patients and socialize with the local gentry. At the insistence of a young disciple who also covered his lodging expenses, Miao offered to revise the formerly published case collections with a much more detailed chapter on the methods of “roasting and processing” (
paozhi
) materia medica. The revised case collection was published in 1622 under Miao’s authorship, and the chapter on pharmaceutical methods was soon reproduced as a monograph, with the title
Paozhi dafa (Great Method of Pharmaceutical Preparation

The pharmaceutical instructions contained in this text targeted not rank-and-file physicians but elite patients themselves, who preferred to prepare the remedies by instructing their own servants at home. It was no coincidence for historian Paul Unschuld to observe that the literature on phar- maceutical processing reached “the peak of interest” at the turn of the seventeenth century.
The textualization of hands-on techniques was motivated by a combination of practical and philosophical interest among elite patients, not professional standardization.

在把业余的药学兴趣提升为独立于一般医学的知识分支方面，缪希雍的同时代人中并非只有他一人。王肯堂（1589年进士）也是金坛人，缪希雍1620年代初曾暂居此地；王肯堂被贬官后成为著名的业余行医者。他常与缪希雍谈论医事，两人有时会诊同一病人。与缪希雍侧重药理学不同，王肯堂更关心通过文本教学改善医疗的整体结果。在他看来，医学作为一门复杂的技艺，由五大科组成：脉、因、病、证、治。前三科对门外汉而言难以掌握，王肯堂却认为可以只关注后两科，因为即使没有良医，病人也能根据症状判断可能的治法。1602年，王肯堂刊行了一部通论性汇编《证治准绳》。他在序中坦言，此书可能因绕过深入探究医学的路径而受到攻击，但他主张，获得良好治疗的直接益处将胜过潜在弊端。《证治准绳》至今仍在印行，是中医从业者的常用参考书。

Miao Xiyong was not alone among his contemporaries in promoting amateur interest in pharmacy as a separate branch of knowledge from general medicine. Wang Kentang (jinshi 1589), also a native of Jintan where Miao Xiyong temporarily resided in the early 1620s, became a renowned amateur practitioner after he was demoted from office. Wang frequently conversed with Miao Xiyong on medical matters, the two men sometimes treating the same patient in consultation with each other. Unlike Miao Xiyong’s focus on pharmacology, Wang was more concerned with improving the overall outcome of medical treatment through textual teaching. For him, medicine, as a complex art, consisted of five major fields (
ke
): pulse-taking (
mo
), etiology (
yin
), pathology (
bing
), symptoms (
zheng
), and treatment (
zhi

). While the former three fields were difficult for a layperson to grasp, Wang considered it possible to focus on the last two fields alone, for even in the absence of a good physician, the patient could identify a probable treatment based on the symptoms. In 1602, Wang published a general compendium titled
Standard Measure for Symptoms and Treatments (Zhengzhi zhunsheng

). In his preface, Wang confessed that the book might be attacked for circumventing the path toward a deep exploration of medicine, yet he argued that the immediate benefits of attaining good treatment would outweigh the potential pitfalls.
Standard Measure
remains in print today as a popular reference for Traditional Chinese Medicine practitioners.
王肯堂把药学与一般医学分开的意愿，也反映在他一部笔记杂集所载的一句随感中。一位朋友问他，若要以本草为入口学习医学，该如何读。王肯堂说：“读本草……勿看其主治。”

在此，王肯堂是以一位优秀儒家哲人的身份说话：他坚持本草首先是理解物性本身的良好资料；读者不必带着把药材付诸实践的迫切需求去读本草。王肯堂把本草与治疗学分为不同研究领域的主张，引起许多年轻学者的共鸣；他们并不自视为行医者，却对药性怀有浓厚兴趣。王肯堂、缪希雍这类人物的吸引力，正在于他们把本草开辟为对理学“性”这一范畴进行纯粹探究的领域，与临床医生追求立竿见影的做法截然不同。这一构想与现代基础科学/应用科学的区分有几分相似。然而，17世纪后期的事物并未朝这个方向发展。

Wang Kentang’s willingness to separate pharmacy from general medicine was also reflected in a casual remark recorded in his collection of miscellaneous notes. A friend asked him how to read bencao as an entry point to the study of medicine. “Easy,” said Wang, “you just skip all the sections that tell you the main indications of the drug.”

Here, Wang spoke as a good Confucian philosopher, who insisted that bencao was first and foremost a good source for understanding the nature of things for its own sake; one need not read bencao with the pressing need to put the materia medica into practice. Wang’s proposal for keeping bencao and therapeutics separate realms of study resonated with many young scholars who did not see themselves as practitioners of medicine, but nevertheless took a keen interest in the nature of drugs. The appeal of figures such as Wang Kentang and Miao Xiyong lies in the way that they carved out bencao as a field of pure inquiry into the neo-Confucian category of nature (
xing

), distinct from the clinician’s pursuit of immediate results. This vision bears some resemblance to the modern distinction between the basic and applied sciences. Yet this was not how things would turn out later in the seventeenth century.
1620年万历朝结束，年轻的天启皇帝把政务托付给亲信的宦官顾问魏忠贤（1568—1627）。魏的官场盟友很快与东林党人在几乎一切政策上——从矿税到边防——发生冲突。一份伪造的黑名单列出108名东林人物，把他们比作通俗小说《水浒传》中的草莽英雄。至少在某些版本的黑名单上，缪希雍以“神医”之名赫然在列。
魏忠贤尤为痛恨的直言官员遭逮捕拷打，许多人死于狱中。1624至1625年的殉难者中包括杨涟（生于1572年）；杨涟早年曾任常熟知县，缪希雍曾与他讨论地方事务。
缪希雍的旧友与赞助人丁元荐也被罢官，于1625年在家去世。东林领袖高攀龙听说秘密警察已奉命来逮捕他，便在家中投湖自尽。

1624年末，东林圈中恐怖气氛正盛，老医缪希雍悄然返回故乡常熟处理一些家事。
在那里，他与毛凤苞（1599—1659，后改名毛晋）交谈；毛是当地与缪氏宗族有亲缘关系的一个家族的年轻继承人。得知缪希雍已完成一部总结其本草理解的论著后，毛晋与几位年轻士人主动相助。成果便是《神农本草经疏》（下称《经疏》），1625年在常熟毛晋的宅第刊行（图3.2a、3.2b）。
正如精英士人在家自制药物，由业余士人撰写、私人刊行的本草文本，在17世纪也将日益普遍。
In late 1624, as terror reigned supreme among Donglin circles, the old physician Miao Xiyong quietly returned to his hometown of Changshu to attend to some family affairs.

While there, he conversed with Mao Fengbao (1599– 1659, who later changed his name to Mao Jin), the young heir to a local family related to Miao’s lineage. Upon learning that Miao Xiyong had completed a treatise that summed up his understanding of bencao, Mao and a few other young literati offered to help. The resulting text,
Exegesis of the Divine Farmer’s Classic of Materia Medica (Shennong bencao jing shu
, hereafter
Exegesis
), was released in print in 1625 from Mao’s residence in Changshu (figures 3.2a and 3.2b).
Just as elite literati prepared their own material remedies at home, private publishing of bencao texts composed by amateur literati would become increasingly common over the seventeenth century.
缪希雍的《经疏》：自然的具体者
Miao Xiyong’s
Exegesis
: Natural Particulars
缪希雍有意让《经疏》成为一部关于本草的激进宣言。在缪希雍看来，官方药典的根本问题在于“言其然而不言其所以然”。

自陶弘景编纂“集注”以来，本草作为官方药典的文本群已不断扩张了一千多年。缪希雍提出，若不能对药物为何如此起作用给出因果解释，本草这一体裁便永远无法超越一团令人困惑的信息拼合。与李时珍不同，缪希雍无意深挖本草文本群在过去数百年中累积的层层注疏，而是要从头提供一个全新的开端。书名中的“疏”字，本义来自“疏浚淤塞之河”，含有向外疏通之意，与西文“exegesis”（疏解）一词的词源相通。不同于为经典文本作注（zhu）、诠释并确定其含义的举动，“疏”力图把经典文本的隐义拉近读者。
缪希雍曾向士人朋友抱怨，《本草纲目》的广博收载实际上进一步把这一主题“踳驳”了，使之臃肿而缺乏决定性论断。
相形之下，《经疏》将“直接”地呈现神农在本草体裁创立之初据以确立药学基本法则的原理。
Miao Xiyong intended
Exegesis

to be a radical statement on the subject of bencao. The fundamental problem with the official pharmacopeia, in Miao’s mind, was that it “talked about how this-is-so without saying why this-should-be-so.”
Since Tao Hongjing compiled the “collected commentary” (
jizhu
), the corpus of bencao had been constantly expanding as an official pharmacopeia for more than a millennium. Without causal explanations of
why

drugs work the way they do, Miao suggested, the genre of bencao could never go beyond a confusing amalgam of information. Unlike Li Shizhen, Miao had no interest in digging through the several layers of commentary that the corpus of bencao had accrued in the previous centuries, but instead offered a fresh beginning from the ground up. The term
shu

in the title, a word originating from the sense of “dredging a flooded river,” connotes an outgoing motion similar to the etymology of “exegesis” (to lead outward). Distinct from the act of adding a commentary (
zhu
) that glosses and ascertains the meaning of a classical text, a shu seeks to bring the hidden meanings of a classical text closer to the reader.
The broad coverage of
Bencao gangmu
, Miao reportedly complained to his literati friends, had in fact further “messed up” (
chuanbo
) the subject, rendering it ponderous and lacking in decisive arguments.
The
Exegesis
, by contrast, would offer “direct access” (
zhijie
) to the principles with which the Divine Farmer had established the basic rules of pharmacy at the very origin of the genre of bencao.

《经疏》刊行于李时珍《本草纲目》之后不到三十年，却只讨论490种常用药，而李时珍收药1,892种；书中既无参考书目，也无插图。本草的缩短也意味着背离药典累积式的格式。正文之前有两篇理论密集的章节，缪希雍在其中阐述其药治原则。每味药的讨论分三节：首先是从《神农本草经》中摘出的该药简略描述，接着是几句构成“疏”的文字。其次，缪希雍设有“主治参互”一节，说明每一具体药物如何应用于特定症状的治疗。最后一节名为“简误”，描述在哪些情况下不应使用该药，以避免不良反应。他所运用的文本策略，与儒家经典的类似疏解文本相通，当时的士人读者对此应当并不陌生。
Published less than three decades after Li Shizhen’s
Bencao gangmu, Exegesis

discussed only 490 kinds of common drugs in contrast to the 1,892 drugs covered by Li Shizhen and included neither a bibliography nor illustrations. The shortening of bencao also involved departing from the accumulative format of the pharmacopeia. Two densely theoretical chapters preceded the main text, in which Miao laid out his principles of pharmacotherapy. The discussion of each drug had three sections: first, the terse description of the drug in question from the
Divine Farmer’s Classic
, followed by a couple of sentences that constituted the “exegesis.” Second, Miao included a section called “main indications for mutual reference” (
zhuzhi canhu
), in which each particular substance was applied to the treatment of specific symptoms. A final section called “errors” (
jianwu
) described situations in which the drug should
not

be administered in order to avoid adverse effects. The textual strategies he employed resembled similar exegetical texts to the Confucian classics, and would have been familiar to literati readers of the day.
《经疏》的议程不止于简单借用理学文本的文体。缪希雍对本草的激进再造，借药学主题对理学关于“性”的论述作出回应。这一问题的重要性体现在缪希雍序言的第一句：“药性之道，具在本草。”
缪希雍汲取金元医家的宇宙论药理学（见第一章），重申物性的形而上学基础：
The agenda of
Exegesis

goes deeper than a simple borrowing of literary styles from neo-Confucian texts. Miao Xiyong’s radical reinvention of bencao used the subject of pharmacy to make a statement on the neo-Confucian nature. The importance of the issue is reflected in the first sentence of Miao’s preface: “the Way of the nature of drugs is completely recorded in
bencao
Drawing from the cosmic pharmacology of Jin-Yuan physicians (see chapter 1), Miao Xiyong reiterated the metaphysical underpinnings to the nature of things:
“夫物之生也，必禀乎天；其成也，必资乎地。天布令，主发生，寒、热、温、凉四时之气行焉，阳也。地凝质，主成物，酸、苦、辛、咸、甘、淡五行之味滋焉，阴也。……物有味，必有气，有气斯有性，自然之道也。”

When a Thing is created, Heaven endorses it; When a Thing is completed, Earth supports it. Heaven gives order, and is in charge of procreation, thus Cold, Hot, Warm and Cool, the qi of four seasons circulates there; this is Yang. Earth condenses matter, and is in charge of substantiation, thus Sour, Bitter, Pungent, Salty, Sweet and Balanced, the taste of Five Phases nourishes there; this is Yin. . . . As a Thing has taste, then it must have qi, and possesses a certain nature. This is simply the Way-as-it-is (
ziran zhi dao
在此，缪希雍所阐述的性论，一方面牢牢立足于理学的性论，另一方面则基于关联性宇宙论的基本信条。朱熹等人只是暗示认识药性的可能，或借药物阐明自己的学说；缪希雍却发誓要探究“自然之道”，以便用气与味这两种基本属性来解释本草的真正教说，而气、味又分别对应宇宙的秩序力量（阴阳二元与五行）。一切资料都必须纳入一个连贯的模式。
Here Miao articulates a view of nature (
xing

) that is firmly situated in the neo-Confucian theory of nature, on the one hand, and the basic tenets of correlative cosmology on the other. Unlike Zhu Xi and others who merely alluded to the possibility of knowing the nature of drugs or who used drugs to illustrate their doctrines, Miao Xiyong vowed to investigate the “way-as-it-is” so that the true teachings of bencao could be explained with two primary qualities, qi and taste, that in turn corresponded to the ordering cosmic forces (the dyad yin/ yang, and the five phases). All data had to fit into a coherent pattern.
例如，大黄一条便体现了缪希雍对单味药作疏的程序。他首先从《神农本草经》中引出大黄的基本属性：
The entry on rhubarb (
dahuang
), for example, exemplifies Miao’s procedure of exegesis for individual drugs. First, he quoted the basic qualities of rhubarb from the
Divine Farmer’s Classic of Materia Medica
“大黄：味苦，寒，大寒，无毒。”
Rhubarb. Taste: bitter. Qi: Cold. Exceedingly Cold. Not Poisonous
接着，他列出陶弘景《集注》所载大黄的全部“主治”：
He then listed all the “main indications” for rhubarb that Tao Hongjing recorded in his
Collected Commentary
“主下瘀血〔1〕。血闭寒热〔2〕。破癥瘕积聚，留饮宿食〔3〕。荡涤肠胃〔4〕。推陈致新，通利水谷〔5〕。调中化食，安和五脏〔6〕。平胃下气〔7〕。除痰实，肠间结热〔8〕。心腹胀满〔9〕。女子寒血闭胀，小腹痛，诸老血留结〔10〕。”

Main indications: Purges congested blood [1]. Stops blood flow and fever [2]. Breaks abdominal bumps and stagnated liquid and food in bowels [3]. Raids and cleanses stomach and bowels [4]. Purges the old and to generate the new. Facilitates passage of water and grains [5]. Mediates the inner body, facilitates digestion, harmonizes the Five Organs [6]. Pacifies the stomach and brings the qi down [7]. Gets rid of phlegm (tan), congested heat amongst the bowels [8]. Treats swelling and fullness in chest and abdomen [9]. Treats women’s obstructed menses, swelling lower abdomen, and misc. stagnation of stale blood [10].

缪希雍不理会后世本草作者卷帙浩繁的注疏，只依据基本属性来工作，以解释《本经》所载十项主治为何应如其所称地起效。他推断，大黄“大寒”之气如冬季下降之气，必然使其药理作用趋向下行，通过有力泻下实现代谢更新（推陈致新）。大黄的“苦”味则与重阴之禀相配，因而对可见的、物质性的血脉流动具有更强亲和力。这样，他便能把大黄之性同本草所载第1至3项主要主治联系起来。他主张，其余各项属于次要症状，也可以用大黄治疗，但必须谨慎考虑病症的生理背景。例如，第6项主治虽表明大黄可用于“调中化食”，缪希雍却提醒读者，这种益处只是次要的，取决于泻下的主要作用。因此，只有当消化不良背后的原因是实滞、而非正气虚损时，才应使用大黄。

Disregarding the voluminous commentaries made by later bencao authors, Miao decided to work only with the basic qualities, so as to explain why the ten recorded indications should work as claimed in the
Classic

. Miao deduced that its “very cold” qi, “just like” the corresponding motion of descending air in winter, necessarily led its pharmacological action to push downward, achieving metabolic renewal through a forceful purge (
tui chen zhi xin

). Rhubarb’s “bitter” taste, in turn, matches it to the heavy yin endowment, which creates a higher affinity toward the visible, material flow of blood vessels. In this way, he was able to link rhubarb’s nature to the main claims 1–3 recorded in the bencao. The rest, he argued, belonged to secondary symptoms that could also be treated with rhubarb, but one had to be careful about the physiological context of the condition. For instance, although claim 6 indicated that rhubarb could be used to “moderate the bowels and facilitate digestion,” Miao warned readers that the benefit was only secondary, depending on the primary action of purging. Thus, it should only be administered in situations when the cause behind indigestion was real blockage, not depletion of vital forces.
缪希雍并非文献学家，他大体把本草文本视为意义透明。当推演陷入死胡同时，他会毫不犹豫地质疑某句话的真实性。例如，干姜被记载能治吐血，缪希雍却断定：姜性味辛、气属温热，其药理作用必然始终是发散（辛味的药理作用见表1.1）与温热的。像干姜这样的温热药，绝无可能治愈吐血——那是体内热盛的明确征兆。
他对本草的处理追求连贯与确定，有时不惜压倒文本证据。

Being no philologist, Miao treated the text of bencao as largely transparent in meaning. When his deductions reached a dead end, he would not hesitate to cast doubt over the authenticity of a sentence. Dried ginger, for instance, was recorded as being able to resolve the vomiting of blood, but Miao decided that since ginger’s nature is pungent in taste and warm or hot in its qi formation, the pharmacological action of ginger should always be dissipating (for pharmacological action of the pungent taste, see table 1.1) and warming. There was simply no way for a warm drug like ginger to cure blood vomiting, a sure sign of excessive heat in the body.
His approach to bencao strove for a coherence and certainty that sometimes overrode textual evidence.
缪希雍处理药物物性的方式，也在对待差异（chabie）与物质多样性的态度上背离了金元药理学（见第一章）。他不再满足于建立宇宙感应的基本原则，而是试图通过逐一考察具体物质的性来确认其真实性。他怀疑，这个简单的体系是否终究无法解释一切：为何有些苦寒药会耗竭体液，另一些却补充体液？为何有些味酸的药性寒，另一些却性热？
更令人困惑的是始终存在的中毒危险：像人参这样看似温良的补药，使用不当也会造成伤害。正如缪希雍在导论性章节中所说：
Miao Xiyong’s approach to pharmaceutical objecthood also departed from Jin-Yuan pharmacology (see chapter 1) in his approach to
differences (chabie

) and material diversity. No longer content with setting up the basic principles of cosmic correspondence, Miao sought to ascertain their veracity by working through the nature of individual substances. He wondered whether the simple system might, after all, fail to explain everything: Why did some drugs that were bitter and cold have the effect of drying up bodily liquids, while others replenished them? Why could some drugs with a sour taste be cold and others hot in nature?
Even more perplexing was the ever-present danger of poisoning, as seemingly benevolent cures like ginseng could do harm when used improperly. As Miao stated in the introductory chapter:
“夫药石禀天地偏至之气者也。虽醇和浓懿，号称上药，然所禀既偏，所至必独。脱也用违其性之宜，则偏重之害，势所必至。”
Medicines are endowed with the idiosyncratic (
pian
) and extreme
qi
of Heaven and Earth. Even the effects of mellow and virtuous supreme drugs, since they still possess idiosyncratic qualities (
pian
), must nevertheless be dangerous. If one uses them in ways inappropriate for their nature, they will inevitably wreak havoc by their idiosyncratic forces.
因此，不仅有必要明确解释药物的“德”，也必须警告人们其潜在危害。药与毒、良性与恶性之间本无固有界限，万物皆有其偏，依情境不同可产生相反的效果。

It was therefore not only necessary to explicitly explain the “virtues” of drugs, but also to warn people of their potential harm. There was no inherent distinction between medicine and poison, or good and bad natures, but all things were idiosyncratic and could exert opposite effects depending on the context.
缪希雍对“偏”（pian，失衡）一词的用法值得仔细注意。在古典医学中，“偏”的问题最常出现在病理语境中，指各脏腑所居的生命力量失去平衡。
例如，《内经》写道，五味各入其所对应的五脏（见表1.1）。当摄入失衡（某一种味吃得过多），某一脏腑系统便会偏胜于其他系统，久而久之成为病态。
中古早期重要的《内经》注家王冰（约活动于762—763年）对这段话的注释是：
Miao Xiyong’s usage of the term
pian

(unbalanced) warrants close attention here. In classical medicine, the issue of pian was most commonly evoked in a pathological context, indicating a loss of balance among the vital forces residing in various organs.
In the
Inner Canon

, for instance, it was written that the consumption of each of the five flavors would feed into one of five main organs to which it corresponded (see table 1.1). When the intake became imbalanced (eating too much of one flavor over others), one organic system would prevail over others and become pathological over time.
Wang Bing (fl. 762–63), an important early medieval commentator on the
Inner Canon
, glossed the paragraph as follows:
“气增不已，益岁年则脏气偏胜；气有偏胜，则有偏绝；脏有偏绝，则有暴夭者。”
If the
qi
[derived from ingested food or medicine] accumulates incessantly, the
qi
of certain organs will overwhelm others (
piansheng
) and result in extreme imbalance (
pianjue
). Once an organ falls into an abrupt imbalance, it will result in sudden death.
总体而言，关于“偏”的医学话语，表达了对过量摄入强效物质可能导致生命之气停滞、壅塞的深切焦虑。凝视的焦点落在身体内部的平衡，而非物质本身。

Overall, the medical discourse of pian denoted a deep anxiety about the stagnation and congestion of vital breath that could result from excessive intake of potent substances. The focus of the gaze fell on the internal balance of the body, not on the substances themselves.
然而，缪希雍对失衡病理的解释，把讨论焦点转向了药物的形而上学构成。“偏性”（pianxing）一词显然源自本章前文所见的理学语境。按照朱熹的性之等级，人高居于万物之上，禀有最完整的性（quan）。然而物性与人性并非截然不同，只是在同一光谱上较不完整（故为“偏”）。人与非人生物因此在彼此身上看到部分的熟悉，而非绝对的差异。
Miao Xiyong’s explanation of the pathologies of imbalance, however, turns the focus of discussion outward to the metaphysical makeup of drugs. The term
pianxing

(imbalanced nature) clearly derived from the neo-Confucian context as we have seen earlier this chapter. According to Zhu Xi’s hierarchical notion of nature, humans were ranked on top of all other creatures as possessing the most complete (
quan

) nature. Yet the nature of things was not categorically different, but merely less complete (hence pian) along a spectrum. Humans and nonhuman creatures thus saw in each other partial familiarity instead of absolute otherness.
在强调人与世界之性相互关联的学派基础上，缪希雍用《经疏》记录药性的差异，并主张这些差异提供了臻于医学卓越的关键洞见。通过模糊良性与毒性药理作用之间的界限，缪希雍指出，每种药的偏性都应结合该生物生命史的具体情境来把握。正是在这个意义上，我把缪希雍本草中的“偏性”解为“偏至之性”（idiosyncratic），而非“失衡之性”。
无穷多样的创造力混合，造就了物的多样性，而这些物又可供人用作药物。换言之，它们是“自然的具体者”（natural particulars）。
Building upon the schools of thought that emphasized the interconnected nature of people and the world, Miao Xiyong used his
Exegesis
to document the
differences

in the nature of drugs that, he argued, offered the key insight to achieve excellence in medicine. By blurring the boundary between benign and poisonous pharmacological actions, Miao pointed out that the pian nature of each medicine should be grasped in the specific circumstances of the creature’s life history. It is in this sense that I translated pianxing in Miao’s bencao as “idiosyncratic” instead of “unbalanced nature.”
An endlessly diverse mixture of creative forces gave rise to the diversity of things, which then lent themselves to be used as medicines. They were, in other words, natural particulars.
据一则充满同情的回忆，缪希雍在壮年时常与东林书院的显要人物宴饮。酒席延续到深夜，众人微醺之际，缪希雍便会起身，激昂陈词，谈论神农失传的教说与当今的道德沦丧。缪希雍主张，医学经典与本草或许正是追回上古失传教说最为可靠的文本遗存。他随即责备这些显赫宾客未能改变现状；听到这番责难，宾客们无不流下悔恨之泪，放声痛哭。

According to one sympathetic recollection, Miao Xiyong in his prime years often dined with luminaries of the Donglin Academy. As the party went on into the late night and everyone became a little drunk, Miao would stand up and give passionate speeches about the lost teachings of the Divine Farmer and the moral degeneration of the present age. If anything, argued Miao, the medical classics and bencao might be the most certain textual remnants from which to retrieve the lost teachings of antiquity. He would then admonish the illustrious guests for failing to change the status quo, and, upon hearing this reproach, the guests would all shed tears of remorse and weep loudly.

一位名医的生涯与一场政治运动最壮观的成败时刻，在缪希雍身上交汇，绝非偶然。在一个对道德确定性怀有深切信念并公开彰显它的时代，缪希雍提出了一种迎合士人兴趣的新本草议程。东林党人虽坚决投身朝政改革，却未能战胜对手。缪希雍骨子里仍是一位秘术之士，令他们印象深刻的不仅是他展示的医术，还有他许诺的对药性的掌握。《经疏》在阐释具体物性时总结了这一讯息：药理作用的能力，成为道德行动能力的微观重演；物质的多样性，则是人性多样性的直接隐喻。尽管东林党人旋即失败并遭迫害，这种情感仍将延续到明朝统治的最后岁月。

The intersection between a master physician’s career and a political movement’s most spectacular moments of triumph and defeat in the person of Miao Xiyong is no coincidence. Miao articulated the agenda for a new type of bencao that was tailored to scholarly interests at a time of deep conviction in, and public display of, moral certainty. Despite their militant commitments to reform court politics, the Donglin partisans failed to prevail over their oppo- nents. At heart still an esoteric magician, Miao Xiyong impressed them not only with his display of medical virtuosity, but with his promised mastery over the nature of drugs.
Exegesis

summed up this message in its explication of particular natures: the capacity for pharmacological action became a microcosmic reenactment of the capacity for moral action; the diversity of matter a direct metaphor for the diversity of humanity. Despite the immediate defeat and persecution of Donglin partisans, this sentiment would last well into the final years of Ming rule.
讲论与讲学：晚明士人科学的社会环境
Discourses and Lectures: The Social Milieu of Late Ming Literati Science
当然，缪希雍对本草的再造所呈现的疏解分析，并非孤身一人的事业。据一则轶事，缪希雍是在船上旅途中，由最亲近的弟子陪同，逐段攻克《经疏》中最难的部分。
在常熟刊行《经疏》的年轻士人毛凤苞，认为此书能给予“中人已上之资”最大益处，正如他自己一样。
毛晋的评论暗示了一个代际转折的时刻：如果东林党的资深创始成员从缪希雍对药性的探究中直接获得灵感，那么在他们后辈中那些“中等”的年轻成员，在1620年代激烈的党争之后，又有哪些选择？
编者说明：底本将这段评价归给毛凤苞；天启五年《神农本草经疏》原刻“梓行本草疏题辞”中有“中人已上之资”，题辞署缪希雍。底本所据其他版本及归属仍待核对。
The exegetical analysis presented in Miao Xiyong’s reinvention of bencao was not, to be sure, a solitary endeavor. According to one anecdote, Miao worked through the most difficult passages of
Exegesis
while traveling on a boat, accompanied by his closest disciples.
Mao Fengbao, the young literatus in Changshu who published
Exegesis
, saw the book as imparting the greatest benefit to people with “middling talent and above” (
zhongren yi shang zhi zi
), just like himself.

Mao’s comment suggested a moment of generational shift: If the senior, founding members of the Donglin partisans found direct inspiration from Miao Xiyong’s inquiry into the nature of drugs, what options did the younger and “middling” members of their lineages have, in the wake of the turbulent partisan politics of the 1620s?
Editor's note (Chinese): 底本将这段评价归给毛凤苞；天启五年《神农本草经疏》原刻“梓行本草疏题辞”中有“中人已上之资”，题辞署缪希雍。底本所据其他版本及归属仍待核对。
一个答案是，东林幸存的追随者不必等太久便等到了报复。1627年，新登基的崇祯皇帝同情东林事业，命魏忠贤自尽，并起复许多东林党人。魏氏旧党与东林之间的冲突贯穿1630、1640年代，江南积极的士人组织新的“社”来集结支持、表达政治议程。
这样看来，随着年轻一代成长，16世纪后期的政治参与与行动主义似乎毫不减弱地延续下来。

One answer was that the surviving followers of Donglin did not have to wait very long for their revenge. In 1627, a new emperor, Chongzhen, was sympathetic to the Donglin cause and reinstated many Donglin partisans to office, after ordering Wei Zhongxian to commit suicide. The conflict between Wei’s former allies and the Donglin lingered through the 1630s and 1640s, and proactive literati in Jiangnan organized new associations (
she
) to rally support and voice their political agenda.
It may seem, then, as if the political participation and activism of the late sixteenth century persisted unabated as the younger generation came of age.

然而细察东林之后的文化生活，事情还有另一面。1620年代的创伤经历或许进一步激励了一些人反击，但也促使另一些人到别处——远离朝中派系斗争——寻求满足与意义。其结果是私人学术与文化再生产的增长，这一趋势在1644年鼎革之后仍延续下来。我们已经遇到过一个例子：毛凤苞（后以毛晋之名著称）。他以缪希雍《经疏》及几部文学选集试手私人出版后，为自己取了一个新的书斋名“汲古阁”，发誓通过刊行各类文本来传播儒家博学。此后二十年间，毛晋刊行了《十三经》与《二十一史》的全套，以及数百种宋元哲学、文学珍本的翻刻本，而始终不求官职。
这种求学与参政的分离，在一个世纪前定会遭到丘濬一类理学政治家的严厉斥责。《大学》所教的神圣而完整的课程，从修身开始，最终通向平天下，如今却沿着一条新出现的断层线碎裂，划出了士人精英私人与公共生活的界线。这一断裂过程在1640年代中期清军入关之前，已变得相当显著。

A closer look at post-Donglin cultural life suggests that there was more to the story. While the traumatic experience of the 1620s may have further galvanized some to fight back, it also encouraged others to seek fulfillment and purpose elsewhere, away from factional struggles at court. This resulted in the growth of private scholarship and cultural reproduction, a trend that would survive the dynastic transition after 1644. One example we have already encountered is Mao Fengbao (later known by the name Mao Jin). Having tried his hand at private publishing with Miao Xiyong’s
Exegesis
and a couple of literary anthologies, Mao refashioned himself with a new studio name,
Jigu ge
(Pavilion of Inspiration from Antiquity), and vowed to propagate Confucian erudition by publishing a wide range of texts. Over the next twenty years, Mao published complete sets of the
Thirteen Confucian Classics
and
Twenty-One Dynastic Histories
, as well as reprints of several hundred rare Song-Yuan philosophical and literary texts, all the while without seeking public office.

This severance between the pursuit of learning and participation in governance would have been severely admonished a century ago by neo-Confucian statesmen like Qiu Jun. The sacred, integral curriculum taught by
Daxue

, one that began with the cultivation of the self and eventually led up to the pacification of the world, fractured along an emerging fault line that demarcated the private and the public lives of literati elite. This process of fissure had already become quite pronounced before the Qing conquest in the mid-1640s.
学问的私人化日益与官方领域疏离，也维持了士人对本草领域的业余兴趣。1620、1630年代的许多本草作者并非政治活动家。相反，我们在他们的著作中察觉到一种意愿：围绕理学意义上对“自然”之学的共同热爱来建立社交圈。在这些圈子里，个人经验的表述被认可为可靠知识的来源。

The privatization of learning, increasingly estranged from the official sphere, also sustained amateur interest in the field of bencao. Many bencao authors of the 1620s and 1630s were not political activists. Instead, we detect in their works a willingness to build social circles around the common love of “natural” studies in the neo-Confucian sense. Within these circles, the articulation of personal experience came to be validated as a reliable source of good knowledge.
1624年，年轻学者倪朱谟完成了一部题为《本草汇言》的论著。倪朱谟出身江南显赫的士人家族；他的族祖倪元璐（1593—1644，1622年进士）为侄孙的本草作序。据底本的叙述，倪元璐称朱谟为一位性情安静、爱好古学的士人，序中丝毫没有本章开头所引罗文英序里的那种怀疑。倪元璐后来在崇祯朝官居高位，竭力主张对东林旧敌报复，1644年北京陷落前夕死去。
倪朱谟曾是一位“埋头场屋”的勤勉学子，却终生没有功名。地方志把他与其他医者一同记载，称其“沉默好古”。
他的本草在他身后于1645年由儿子刊行。
编者说明：底本称倪元璐在序中将倪朱谟描述为好古而安静的人；所见《本草汇言》倪元璐序的数字转录未见此语，尚需核对底本所据版本。后文“沉默好古”则引自地方志，不能径作序文原话。
In 1624, a young scholar named Ni Zhumo completed a treatise titled
Collected Discourse of Bencao (Bencao huiyan

). Ni was descended from a prominent Jiangnan literati clan; a grand uncle of his, Ni Yuanlu (1593–1644, jinshi 1622), wrote a preface for his nephew’s bencao. Describing Zhumo as a “quiet man who loves antiquity,” Ni Yuanlu expressed none of the skepticism in Luo Wenying’s preface quoted at the beginning of this chapter. Ni Yuanlu would go on to hold high office in the Chongzhen reign, lobbying hard for revenge on the former enemies of Donglin, and die at the eve of the fall of Beijing in 1644.
Once a diligent student who “buried his head in preparing for the civil service examination” (
mai shou changwu
), Ni Zhumo lived the rest of his life degree-less. He was remembered, along with other medical physicians in the local gazetteer, as someone “quiet in nature” (
xing chenmo
) with a “love for antiquity” (
haogu
His bencao was published posthumously in 1645 by his son.
Editor's note (Chinese): 底本称倪元璐在序中将倪朱谟描述为好古而安静的人；所见《本草汇言》倪元璐序的数字转录未见此语，尚需核对底本所据版本。后文“沉默好古”则引自地方志，不能径作序文原话。
由于没有仕宦履历，他的本草文本便成了我们了解倪朱谟生平的唯一资料。在书中，倪朱谟同意缪希雍的批评，认为李时珍对药典的系统重组缺乏学术严谨性。他也相信通过严密推理理解药性是可能的。
然而此书最引人注目之处，是“汇言”的社会性格。为撰写此书，倪朱谟“部邑市廛，幽岩隐谷”，寻访本草方面的专家与文献。他前后咨询了一百多位对话者（包括学者、医者与博学僧侣），并把交谈整理成文。在他访谈过的人中，他尊十二人为“师资”，缪希雍名列第三；他又列出136位“同社”，仔细记下他们的姓名与籍贯。倪朱谟认为他们都是“皆万历时人，一时名俊耆儒深明于医者”。
这些人大多来自下江地区，也有一些来自北方与西部。此书表明，在晚明，对药性的共同兴趣——而非家族或政治议程——成了志同道合士人之间的社会黏合剂。

Lacking a track record in an official career, the text of his bencao therefore remains the only source through which we can recover any information about Ni Zhumo’s life. In it, Ni agreed with Miao Xiyong in criticizing Li Shizhen’s systematic reorganization of the pharmacopeia as lacking in scholarly rigor. He also believed in the possibility of understanding the nature of drugs through rigorous reasoning.

Yet the most remarkable feature of this text is the social character of the “collected discourse.” To compose this book, Ni Zhumo traveled “through cities and markets, and over the quiet and hidden mountain valleys,” seeking out experts and texts on the subject of bencao. Altogether, he consulted more than a hundred interlocutors (including scholars, physicians, and learned monks) and compiled these exchanges into written form. Of the people he interviewed, he acknowledged twelve as mentors (
shizi
), among whom Miao Xiyong ranked in third place. He also listed 136 fellow scholars (
tongshe
), whose names and hometowns he carefully recorded. Ni considered them all “remarkable Confucian scholars active during the Wanli reign, also deeply learned in medicine.”

The majority of these people were from the Lower Yangzi area, although some did hail from the north and west. The book shows that in late Ming times, a common interest in the nature of drugs, rather than familial or political agendas, became a social glue among like-minded literati.

另一个学术交往的中心是杭州，这座风景如画的省城位于下江三角洲南侧（见地图0.1插图）。包括“武林诸君子”在内的名士官员，常出入于卢复的家。卢复没有功名，也从未追求仕途。卢家显然享有足够的声望与富足，使卢复以慷慨资助医学学生、推动医术而闻名。他的儿子卢之颐继承了对于医学与佛教的热爱。据卢之颐自己回忆，他常静坐于父亲主持的讲会中，听学者辩论古典医学与大乘佛教的难题。有一天，平日寡言的卢之颐站起身来，令众人惊讶地向一位资深宾客提出一连串尖锐的诘问，挑战对方让出讲席。此后，卢之颐作为真正神童的名声很快超过父亲，父子二人开始合作撰写一部新的本草论著。

Another hub of scholarly association was Hangzhou, the picturesque provincial capital located on the southern side of the Lower Yangzi Delta (map 0.1 inset). Famous literati and officials, including “many gentlemen of Wulin [Hangzhou]” (
Wulin zhu junzi

) frequented the house of Lu Fu, a man who held no degrees and never pursued an official career. The Lu family apparently enjoyed enough respect and prosperity that Lu Fu became known for his generosity toward students of medicine and the advancement of this art. His son Lu Zhiyi inherited a love for medicine and Buddhism. In his own recollection, Lu Zhiyi described how he used to sit quietly at the lectures hosted by his father, listening to scholars debating difficult issues in classical medicine and Mahayana Buddhism. One day, the usually reticent Lu Zhiyi stood up and, to everyone’s surprise, posed a string of sharp and challenging questions to a senior guest, challenging the latter to yield the lectern to him. After that, Lu Zhiyi’s fame as a real prodigy soon exceeded that of his father’s, and they started to collaborate on a new treatise of bencao.
卢复与卢之颐都高度推崇李时珍的《本草纲目》，把它用作系统性的相关资料汇编。他们也熟悉缪希雍的《经疏》，时常引用。缪希雍在下江地区过着游历生活；卢家则不同，他们以杭州的家宅为固定场所，发展出一个广泛的本草学者网络。卢复去世后，卢之颐继续撰写他们的本草，并通过公开辩论检验自己的见解，同时为慕名而来的病人诊病。
他的本草稿本是一部浸透禅宗术语的哲学论著，到1640年代初已接近完成，杭州家中的书斋也开始认真雕版准备刊行。

Lu Fu and Lu Zhiyi both had high praise for Li Shizhen’s
Bencao gangmu
, which they used as a systematic collection of relevant sources. They were also familiar with Miao Xiyong’s
Exegesis

and frequently referred to it. Unlike Miao, who led a peripatetic life in the Lower Yangzi region, the Lu family used their Hangzhou home as a stable venue to develop a wide-ranging network of bencao scholars. After Lu Fu passed away, Lu Zhiyi continued to work on their bencao and tested his ideas through public debate, all the while treating patients who were attracted by his growing fame.

His bencao manuscript, a philosophical treatise infused with Chan Buddhist terms, was near completion in the early 1640s, and the carving of woodblocks for publishing started in earnest at his home studio in Hangzhou.

客曰：吾见竹叶一岁成，二岁茂，三岁密，至四岁则细，五岁疏，六岁瘁矣。未见有至六十岁而华者。

颐曰：古人盖指……根历一元而言，不但举一茎之荣枯已也。

客曰：竹节生时已具，安见其与四时合耶？

颐曰：冬半而孕，春半而生，夏半而代叶，秋半而引根，四气历然，非独以出土之时为生也。

Guest: As far as I can see, bamboo grows leaves in Year One, becomes lush in Year Two, dense in Year Three, emaciates in Year Four, then becomes further sparse in Year Five before it dies in Year Six. How can there be such thing as flowering every sixty years?

Yi [Lu Zhiyi]: The ancient author meant that the bamboo root could live for a Sexagenary Cycle, not just referring to the growth and death of one stalk.

Guest: Bamboo has knots as soon as it is born. How is it that its growth fits the seasonal cycle?

Yi: Bamboo prepares its bud in mid-winter, grows out in mid-spring, changes its leaves in mid-summer, and elongates its root in mid-autumn—how clear is its seasonal punctuation! “Growth” should not be understood merely as penetration of the earth.
卢之颐在手稿中把这段对话记入竹条之下，归入他称为“参”的一节。这里，“客”就《神农本草经》的字面含义向卢之颐发问，而卢之颐在这个例子中设法找到了一个可信的解释。
In his manuscript, Lu recorded this conversation in the entry for the bamboo plant, under the section he called “Meditation” (

与缪希雍《经疏》简洁的文笔相比，卢复、卢之颐更热衷于把另一批文学性与非医学文献纳入他们的形而上学思辨。唐宋本草药典把文学资料与医学指示并列，却从未严格地交叉审查二者。卢之颐却认为，对名称（ming）的文献学研究包含着阐明药性的钥匙。

ming

On the question of bamboo leaves, for instance, he speculates that:
“竹者，物之有筋节者也。故筋节字皆从竹。”
Bamboo is a thing that has sinews and knots. That is why the characters for “sinew” (

Lu Zhiyi rejoiced in the abundance of signs in the world. In one move, he conflated the actual bamboo plant with the character for “bamboo,” which in turn appeared as a signifying part in composite characters that meant “sinew” and “knot”:
“茎有节，节有枝，枝必三，枝复有节，若三候成节也。故主候失符节，致令气逆气溢，……致令筋急焦渴也。”
Bamboo has knots on the stalk, and its branches grow out from the knots. The knot repeats itself after three branching points, just like three five-day periods makes up of a solar period (
jie
). Therefore, bamboo cures the overflow of
qi
caused by loss of punctual rhythm, or anxiety brought by overly rigid sinews.
竹的特性还可以用更多方式解读，并与它的药效联系起来：
There are still more ways in which the characteristics of the bamboo plant can be deciphered and associated with its medicinal properties:
“实通神明，轻身益气者，竹六十岁始华，穷历支干变化故也。”
Its fruit is conducive to divinity, and lightens the body, because bamboo blooms into flowers every sixty years, that is a full cycle of stem-branch combinations.
此处，六十这个数字因一个甲子——即天干十与地支十二完整配合一周——而具有意义，又被赋予了神圣完满的额外含义。卢之颐想象，食用罕见的竹实，能使疲惫胀满的身体复归宁静。

Here the number sixty, significant due to the sexagenary cycle that contained a complete run of combinations between the ten heavenly stems and the twelve earthly branches of the Chinese calendar, assumed the added meaning of divine perfection. By eating the rare fruit of bamboo, Lu imagined that it would return a body’s tired and turgid constitution to tranquility.
除了丰富的非医学文献依据，卢之颐也从自己的观察中汲取很多。在题为“核”的一节中，他超越本草药典对形态的描述，强调“看”（kan）的重要，因为提示药性的重要迹象可能就藏在显眼之处。在菖蒲一条中，卢之颐观察到：

Its leaves begin to grow from within the stalk, and therefore one can discern its opening effect on the heart vessels. The twisted shape of its stalk and branches is a perfect match for the shape of the conduits that wrap around the heart. 卢之颐的本草诠释学就这样在文本与感官之间摆动，随其所需而诉诸关联思维与术数。他在谈话中作出的自由联想，意在折服对话者。有访客质疑他“何得故为奇特”，卢之颐回答说，“物体性情”必须通过出人意料的读法来把握，否则便会被文字最平庸的含义所缚（fu）。
卢之颐本草的大胆，使他得以把直接观察纳入理解自然及其一切偏至显现的有效资料。药性不仅连贯，而且令人神迷。

Lu’s hermeneutics of bencao thus oscillated between texts and senses, resorting to correlative thinking and numerology as he saw fit. The free-flowing associations he made in conversations were designed to impress his interlocutors. In response to a visitor’s accusation that he was “deliberately seeking strange explanations,” Lu Zhiyi replied that the “embodied nature and preferences of things” (
wu ti xing qing

reading

fu

The audacity of Lu Zhiyi’s bencao allowed him to include direct observation as valid data for the understanding of nature in all its idiosyncratic manifestations. The nature of drugs was not only coherent but also ecstatic.
李中梓的综合课程：业余主义及其批评者
Li Zhongzi’s Integrated Curriculum: Amateurism and its Discontents
在士人结社、公开讲会与雅集清谈中，本草成了受过教育之人的时尚话题，尤其是1620、1630年代成长起来的那一代人。阅读与撰写本草成为一种体面的消遣，甚至职业。在修辞上，研究药性被认为与理学追求道德真理相一致。然而在实践中，年轻士人推崇的是能够保全、维持自身生命的技术，却未必会把这条生命献给更高的目的。

In literati associations, open lectures, and elegant conversations, bencao became a fashionable topic for educated men, especially the generation who came of age in the 1620s and 1630s. The reading and writing of bencao became a respectable pastime, and even occupation. In rhetoric, studying the nature of drugs was considered congruent with the neo-Confucian pursuit of moral truth. Yet in practice, younger literati championed techniques that could safeguard and maintain their own lives, but would not necessarily go on to offer that life for a higher purpose.
由于主题日益流行，本草文本的出版市场在1620至1640年代繁荣起来。《本草纲目》1596年初刻本的雕版起初销路不佳，1640年却被至少两家书坊重新利用，配上新序刊行新版。
16世纪中叶陈嘉谟的本草启蒙书原是无图的白文，1620年代又增补插图，进一步扩充。1621年，苏州还出现了更花哨的食疗本草，由文化商人钱允治拼凑而成，据英文底本，他自称没有学过医，却擅长编辑。
晚明几十年间，旧版翻新、公然剽窃与伪造作者署名层出不穷，芭芭拉·福尔克玛（Barbara Volkmar）对医者万全畅销儿科医书的研究即为显例。
1634年，苏州另一家书坊以李时珍的伪托署名推销自己的食疗本草，甚至伪造了一篇李时珍序，钤上私人印章。伪李时珍声称，继《本草纲目》成功之后，他乐于再向读书界呈上一部食疗之作。他向潜在买家保证，无论气候、地域如何不同，此卷都能帮助他们过上自由无忧、吃饱喝足的生活。

The publishing market for bencao texts flourished in the 1620s to 1640s as a result of rising popularity of the subject matter. The original woodblocks of
Bencao gangmu
’s first edition in 1596, which sold poorly at first, were recycled by at least two publishing houses in 1640 to issue new editions with new prefaces.

The mid-sixteenth-century bencao primer by Chen Jiamo, originally a plain text with no illustrations, was further expanded with added illustrations in the 1620s. Still fancier editions of dietetic bencao emerged from Suzhou in 1621, cobbled together by Qian Yunzhi, a cultural entrepreneur who declared himself as “having learned no medicine, but good at editorial matters.”

The rebranding of previous editions, plain plagiarism, and false attribution of authorship abounded in the late Ming decades, as exemplified by Barbara Volkmar’s study of physician Wan Quan’s bestselling pediatric medical texts.

In 1634, a different Suzhou publisher promoted its own dietetic bencao under the fake authorship of Li Shizhen, even fabricating a preface in Li’s name, complete with personal seals. The pseudo-Li Shizhen claimed that following on
Bencao gangmu

’s success, he was happy to bring a second volume on dietetics to the reading world. He reassured potential buyers that this volume would help them live well “under all climates, in Chinese or foreign lands . . . roaming about free of worry, with a full belly!”

业余士人与商业出版的联盟，就这样创造出一个几十年前的作者难以想象的财富与名声的纽带。对自我的照护名义上是道德行为的源泉，如今却成了以职业作家、鉴赏家或文化批评家身份获取名望的机会。这个时代最成功的人物之一陈继儒（1558—1639），为1634年版食疗本草又写了一篇序。陈继儒以其标志性的机智文笔自称“老饕”，劝诱读者领会本草的重要。以下据英文底本译述：

The alliance between amateur literati and commercial publishing thus created a nexus of wealth and fame unimaginable to authors several decades earlier. The care of the self, nominally the fountainhead of moral behavior, now became an opportunity for achieving celebrity status as a professional author, aesthete, or cultural critic. One of the most successful figures in this age, Chen Jiru (1558–1639), offered another preface for the 1634 edition of the dietetic bencao. In his signature witty prose, Chen declared himself an “old gourmet” (
laotao
), and cajoled the reader to appreciate the importance of bencao:
医生掌握人的性命。与其把性命交给他们任意摆布，何不把命运握在自己手中？日常生活和饮食调养，确实是我自己做主的领域。知道真正的滋味，就会懂得节制；懂得节制，身心便都会安好。

Physicians (

) are those who control people’s lives. Rather than entrusting my life to their whims, why not take my fate into my own hands? Everyday needs and dietetics are indeed a realm where I am in charge. If you know the true flavors, you will know temperance; knowing temperance, your body and mind will be both fine.

推销这部新食疗本草时，有两条看似矛盾的理据在起作用：一方面，伪托李时珍之名借用了医学权威；另一方面，此书更直接的吸引力在于许诺一种无忧而饱足的生活，让人自己掌握命运。对美的欣赏也延伸到本草：1640年，杭州最有办法的出版者之一钱蔚起重刻《本草纲目》江西本（1603），配以新雕插图。
据底本，他在序中称赞工匠的灵巧与对动植物的精妙描绘，使这一新版足以令李时珍之作重焕生气。
钱蔚起坦然谈论自己投入本草的资本，力图把愉悦与美注入对物性的学术探究。

Two seemingly contradictory rationales are at work in marketing this new dietetic bencao: on the one hand, the fake authorship of Li Shizhen invoked medical authority; on the other hand, however, the more immediate appeal of the book resided in the promise of a worry-free, well-fed life, where one would “take one’s fate in his own hands.” The appreciation of beauty extended to bencao as well; in 1640, Qian Weiqi, one of the most resourceful publishers in Hangzhou, reprinted the Jiangxi edition (1603) of
Bencao gangmu
with newly carved illustrations.
In his preface, Qian praised their artisans’ dexterity and masterful depiction of plants and animals, so much so that this new edition would “revitalize” Li’s work.
Talking candidly about the capital he invested in bencao, Qian sought to inject pleasure and beauty into the scholarly inquiry of the nature of things.

医学文本市场的繁荣，受益者不止业余士人作者。1618年，另一部医学论著迅速获得成功，或许要归功于它雅致的书名《颐生微论》。然而作者李中梓（1588—1655）并未吟咏生命的愉悦。李中梓成长于长江三角洲末端、靠近今日上海的一处卫所。朱元璋建立明朝时，他的祖先作为军户被迁到那里。他的祖父与叔伯是1550年代中期剿倭战斗中阵亡的军官；他的父亲幼年成孤，苦读文武两途，渴望显达，却在1589年考中令人艳羡的进士后不久病逝。
李中梓当时尚是孩童，把这一损失铭记于心，立志学好医学。
The flourishing market of medical texts benefited more than amateur literati authors. In 1618, another medical treatise enjoyed quick success, possibly owing to its elegant title,
Subtle Discourses on the Preservation of Life (Yisheng weilun

). The author, Li Zhongzi (1588–1655), however, did not wax lyrical on the pleasures of life. Li had grown up in a military garrison located at the tip of the Yangzi Delta, near modern-day Shanghai. His ancestors had been relocated there as soldiers when Zhu Yuanzhang founded the Ming dynasty. His grandfather and uncles were officers killed in pirate battles in the mid-1550s; his father, orphaned at a young age, studied hard for both civil and military examinations and aspired to greatness, only to take ill and die shortly after winning the coveted jinshi degree in 1589.
Still a boy, Li Zhongzi took the loss to heart and became determined to study medicine well.
尽管书名指向自我修习，《颐生微论》却确立了“医宗”（yizong）的核心地位，为学医者开列了一份标准书目。他的“医学源流”名单只承认神农为本草的第一作者，略去了后世药典的众多注家。在专论药学的一篇短章中，李中梓只选了140种药，坚持“药繁则惑”。
换言之，李中梓试图把医学正统与包罗万象的本草文本群分开，并对药典中哪些部分与临床医者相关施加某种控制。
Despite its reference to the cultivation of the self,
Subtle Discourses on the Preservation of Life
posited the centrality of a “medical orthodoxy” (
yizong

) that set forth a standard reading list for students of medicine. His list of “medical lineages” only endorsed the Divine Farmer as the first author of bencao, while leaving out the numerous commentators on later pharmacopeias. In a short chapter devoted to the subject of pharmacy, Li selected only 140 drugs, insisting that “abundance begets confusion” (
fan ze huo

In other words, Li attempted to dissociate the orthodoxy of medicine from the all-encompassing corpus of bencao and to exert some control over which parts of the pharmacopeia were deemed relevant for a practicing physician.
《微论》成功不久，李中梓又推出第二部畅销文本，这次专论药学。1622年，《药性解》由积极推销食疗本草的钱允治刊行。钱允治抓住金元药学启蒙书的持久流行，把李中梓的文本包装为对著名《药性赋》（见第一章）的现代注解，并作为雷公炮制手册的配套读物。据底本，钱允治认为李中梓的新注胜过众多药性刻本，因为其解释透彻，而又简短全面。
李中梓在自序中慨叹医学自古以来的退化。他写道：“儒者又好自张大，置医于九流之中。”
如果医者如此被轻视、不被尊重，又怎能指望有效的治疗？
Shortly after the success of
Subtle Discourses
, Li produced a second popular text, this time dedicated to the subject of pharmacy. In 1622,
Explanation of the Nature of Drugs (Yaoxing jie

) was published by Qian Yunzhi, the same man who aggressively marketed dietetic bencao. Picking up on the long-lasting popularity of Jin-Yuan pharmacology primers, Qian packaged Li’s text as a modern gloss on the well-known

(see chapter 1) and an accompaniment to the
Master Thunder

manuals on pharmaceutical processing. Li’s new commentary, wrote Qian, was superior to the “abundant imprints on pharmacology” in that it was thorough in its explanation and yet short and comprehensive.
In his own preface, Li lamented the degree to which medicine had degenerated since ancient times. “Confucians like to self-aggrandize” (
ru zhe hao zi zhangda
), he wrote, “and put physicians into the Nine Currents [of minor professions].”
How can one expect effective cures if physicians were so dismissed and disrespected?

李中梓与缪希雍的差异，揭示了17世纪初本草著作多样化中的一个重要问题。两人都未声称出自某位医家嫡传，都涉猎佛教与秘术，也都通过为士人家庭诊病而建立良医声誉。缪希雍在1620年代已在东林党人中享有极高声望，其《经疏》以毛凤苞一类年轻士人读者为对象；这些人乐于玩味关于物性的复杂而微妙的讨论。相形之下，李中梓是一位出身军户、冉冉升起的年轻作者，从未完全认同士大夫的价值观。他把父亲受挫的仕途视为官场危险的证据，很快以医学正统的新捍卫者自居。他多产的著作以简明透明的文笔吸引更广泛的读者，始终把药学论著的范围限定在二三百种药物之内。1637年，李中梓又在《医宗必读》中更明确地重复了这一讯息。
据底本所引方志，借此，他得以使高傲的士人俯首，乘舟车不断前来造访。

The difference between Li Zhongzi and Miao Xiyong belied an important issue in the diversification of bencao works in early seventeenth century. Both men claimed no direct lineage from a medical master, dabbled in Buddhism and esoteric arts, and established their reputations as effective physicians by treating patients in literati families. Miao Xiyong in the 1620s had already enjoyed a highly prominent career among the Donglin partisans and targeted his
Exegesis

at young literati readers, such as Mao Fengbao, who took delight in complexity and subtle discussions about the nature of things. In contrast, Li Zhongzi was an up-and-coming young author who hailed from a military lineage and never fully identified with the values of scholar-officials. He took the thwarted political career of his father as evidence of the perils of officialdom and quickly identified himself as the new champion of medical orthodoxy. His prolific writings appealed to a wider audience with simple, transparent prose, always limiting the scope of his pharmacy treatises to a small number of 200–300 drugs. Later in 1637, Li repeated the message more explicitly with another treatise titled
Must Reads for the Medical Orthodoxy (Yizong bidu
In this way, he was able to bring the haughty literati to his heels, their “boats and carriages ceaselessly docked at his door.”

如我在导论中所论，儒家业余主义的可能性，取决于其他职业的非政治化（用扬雄的话说，工匠不通人事）。晚明见证了儒家士人的进一步主张：要证明自己在专业领域实际上优于技术专家。依据理学性论对本草的激进改造，使业余者得以宣称对药学拥有权威。李中梓的讯息对缪希雍及其他业余作者那种自由炫技的作风，构成了批判立场。如果仅凭对药性的深刻理解，任何人都能发明、提出前所未有的新治法与新解释，那么专家医者与业余哲人之间还有什么区别？

As I have discussed in the introduction, the possibility of Confucian amateurism depended on the depoliticization of other professions (according to Yang Xiong, “artisans do not comprehend human affairs”). Late Ming times witnessed a further assertion by Confucian literati to prove that they were, in fact, better than technical experts in their professional domains. The aggressive refashioning of bencao according to neo-Confucian theories of nature allowed amateurs to claim authority over the science of pharmacy. Li Zhongzi’s message posed a critical stance toward the free-wheeling demonstration of virtuosity by Miao Xiyong and other amateur authors. If, based on a deep understanding of the nature of drugs, anyone could invent and propose new treatments and interpretations that had never existed before, what, then, would be the difference between an expert healer and an amateur philosopher?
然而最终，1630、1640年代的现实是：无论业余士人还是技术专家，都无法从自己的知识中获得多少在公共事务中的有效权力。我们此时听到其他人的愤怒抗议——例如江西地方教育家宋应星对技术未能实现其转化潜能的挫败。
尽管李中梓成功成为畅销书作者，他也抱怨说，虽然自视不止于一个拥有“专门学”的人，自己的成功却把他困在名医的狭窄形象中。据底本引述，像父亲一样，他有时梦想以所学探究天人之理、参悟禅宗隐秘并参与国家事务的商议，然而人们却拉着他的手臂强求，只是为了换取少量药物。
我们大可以把1644年明朝的覆亡，看作技术知识正当所有权长期僵持的结果。

In the end, however, the reality of the 1630s and 1640s was that neither amateur literati nor technical experts could derive much effective power in public affairs from their knowledge. We hear angry protests from others at this time—for example, the Jiangxi local educator Song Yingxing’s frustration over the unfulfilled transformative potential of technology.
For all his success in becoming a bestselling author, Li Zhongzi also complained that while he saw himself as more than someone with “expert skills” (
zhuanmen xue

), his own success had confined him in the narrow image of a master physician. Like his father, he sometimes dreamed of using his knowledge to “investigate Heaven and Humanity, meditate on the hidden secrets of Zen, and consult in affairs of state,” and yet people “held my arms and forced me” in exchange for “a small dose of drugs.”
We might well see the downfall of the Ming in 1644 as a result of the prolonged impasse over the legitimate ownership of technical knowledge.
